This step includes checking for missing values and duplicate records, standardizing variable formats, and converting the dataset from a long format to a wide format. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # check duplicate records df %>% count(country, year, month, category) %>% filter(n > 1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # 2.4 Cluster and Outlier Analysis Module # ## 2.4.1 Country Trade Behaviour Segmentation Country-level features are created to summarise the overall trade behaviour of each country. The clustering result is then used to compare countries across different trade profile groups. Step 1: Create country-level features Monthly observations are aggregated into country-level summary features. These variables capture trade scale, balance, ratio, and variability. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} country_features <- df_wide %>% group_by(country) %>% summarise( avg_input = mean(input, na.rm = TRUE), avg_output = mean(output, na.rm = TRUE), avg_balance = mean(trade_balance, na.rm = TRUE), avg_ratio = mean(trade_ratio, na.rm = TRUE), sd_input = sd(input, na.rm = TRUE), sd_output = sd(output, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop" ) ``` ::: Step 2: Check the feature table The feature is to confirm that the variables are created correctly. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} glimpse(country_features) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Rows: 9 Columns: 7 $ country "china", "china-hk", "china-tw", "japan", "malaysia", "sou… $ avg_input 4260.3402, 421.4964, 3130.9586, 2523.6210, 4362.6608, 1930… $ avg_output 4569.523, 4419.304, 1792.862, 1835.328, 4624.194, 1604.373… $ avg_balance 309.1832, 3997.8078, -1338.0969, -688.2928, 261.5333, -326… $ avg_ratio 1.0357124, 12.0331394, 0.6850890, 0.7400545, 1.0762041, 0.… $ sd_input 1820.1913, 144.3207, 2182.8767, 404.1574, 1026.4777, 875.8… $ sd_output 2192.8041, 1615.5752, 1109.6276, 299.0476, 931.7935, 544.9… ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} head(country_features) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 7 country avg_input avg_output avg_balance avg_ratio sd_input sd_output 1 china 4260. 4570. 309. 1.04 1820. 2193. 2 china-hk 421. 4419. 3998. 12.0 144. 1616. 3 china-tw 3131. 1793. -1338. 0.685 2183. 1110. 4 japan 2524. 1835. -688. 0.740 404. 299. 5 malaysia 4363. 4624. 262. 1.08 1026. 932. 6 south_korea 1931. 1604. -326. 0.905 876. 545. ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} summary(country_features) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` country avg_input avg_output avg_balance Length:9 Min. : 356.7 Min. :1128 Min. :-1338.1 Class :character 1st Qu.:1052.1 1st Qu.:1604 1st Qu.: -688.3 Mode :character Median :2523.6 Median :1835 Median : 261.5 Mean :2459.0 Mean :2764 Mean : 304.9 3rd Qu.:4092.1 3rd Qu.:4419 3rd Qu.: 531.1 Max. :4362.7 Max. :4624 Max. : 3997.8 avg_ratio sd_input sd_output Min. : 0.6851 Min. : 144.3 Min. : 299.0 1st Qu.: 0.8301 1st Qu.: 268.2 1st Qu.: 576.1 Median : 1.0357 Median : 875.9 Median : 931.8 Mean : 2.4772 Mean : 895.9 Mean : 992.7 3rd Qu.: 1.5168 3rd Qu.:1099.2 3rd Qu.:1109.6 Max. :12.0331 Max. :2182.9 Max. :2192.8 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} colSums(is.na(country_features)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` country avg_input avg_output avg_balance avg_ratio sd_input 0 0 0 0 0 0 sd_output 0 ``` ::: ::: Step 3: Prepare the clustering data The country identifier is removed and the numeric variables are standardised before clustering. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cluster_data <- country_features %>% select(where(is.numeric)) cluster_data_scaled <- scale(cluster_data) ``` ::: Step 4: Run clustering In this prototype, countries are segmented into three clusters using k-means clustering. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(123) km3 <- kmeans(cluster_data_scaled, centers = 3, nstart = 25) country_features$cluster <- as.factor(km3$cluster) head(country_features) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 8 country avg_input avg_output avg_balance avg_ratio sd_input sd_output cluster 1 china 4260. 4570. 309. 1.04 1820. 2193. 1 2 china-hk 421. 4419. 3998. 12.0 144. 1616. 3 3 china-tw 3131. 1793. -1338. 0.685 2183. 1110. 1 4 japan 2524. 1835. -688. 0.740 404. 299. 2 5 malaysia 4363. 4624. 262. 1.08 1026. 932. 1 6 south_k… 1931. 1604. -326. 0.905 876. 545. 2 ``` ::: ::: Step 5: Append cluster labels and inspect results The cluster labels are appended back to the country-level feature table for interpretation and plotting. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} head(country_features) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 8 country avg_input avg_output avg_balance avg_ratio sd_input sd_output cluster 1 china 4260. 4570. 309. 1.04 1820. 2193. 1 2 china-hk 421. 4419. 3998. 12.0 144. 1616. 3 3 china-tw 3131. 1793. -1338. 0.685 2183. 1110. 1 4 japan 2524. 1835. -688. 0.740 404. 299. 2 5 malaysia 4363. 4624. 262. 1.08 1026. 932. 1 6 south_k… 1931. 1604. -326. 0.905 876. 545. 2 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} summary(country_features) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` country avg_input avg_output avg_balance Length:9 Min. : 356.7 Min. :1128 Min. :-1338.1 Class :character 1st Qu.:1052.1 1st Qu.:1604 1st Qu.: -688.3 Mode :character Median :2523.6 Median :1835 Median : 261.5 Mean :2459.0 Mean :2764 Mean : 304.9 3rd Qu.:4092.1 3rd Qu.:4419 3rd Qu.: 531.1 Max. :4362.7 Max. :4624 Max. : 3997.8 avg_ratio sd_input sd_output cluster Min. : 0.6851 Min. : 144.3 Min. : 299.0 1:4 1st Qu.: 0.8301 1st Qu.: 268.2 1st Qu.: 576.1 2:4 Median : 1.0357 Median : 875.9 Median : 931.8 3:1 Mean : 2.4772 Mean : 895.9 Mean : 992.7 3rd Qu.: 1.5168 3rd Qu.:1099.2 3rd Qu.:1109.6 Max. :12.0331 Max. :2182.9 Max. :2192.8 ``` ::: ::: Step 6:Visualising results The first chart shows the number of countries in each cluster. This provides an overview of how countries are distributed across the selected groups. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_table1 <- country_features %>% count(cluster) p1 <- ggplot(plot_table1, aes(x = cluster, y = n, fill = cluster)) + geom_col() + labs( title = "Number of Countries in Each Cluster", x = "Cluster", y = "Count" ) + theme_minimal() ggplotly(p1) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: The second chart compares the main trade characteristics across clusters. This helps users understand how the groups differ in terms of average trade behaviour. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_table2 <- country_features %>% group_by(cluster) %>% summarise( avg_input = mean(avg_input, na.rm = TRUE), avg_output = mean(avg_output, na.rm = TRUE), avg_balance = mean(avg_balance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop" ) %>% pivot_longer( cols = c(avg_input, avg_output, avg_balance), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value" ) p2 <- ggplot(plot_table2, aes(x = variable, y = value, fill = cluster)) + geom_col(position = "dodge") + labs( title = "Average Input, Output and Balance by Cluster", x = "Variable", y = "Value" ) + theme_minimal() ggplotly(p2) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ``` ``` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_table3 <- country_features %>% group_by(cluster) %>% summarise( avg_ratio = mean(avg_ratio, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop" ) p3 <- ggplot(plot_table3, aes(x = cluster, y = avg_ratio, fill = cluster)) + geom_col() + labs( title = "Average Trade Ratio by Cluster", x = "Cluster", y = "Average Trade Ratio" ) + theme_minimal() ggplotly(p3) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} country_features %>% select(country, avg_input, avg_output, avg_ratio, cluster) %>% arrange(desc(avg_ratio)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 9 × 5 country avg_input avg_output avg_ratio cluster 1 china-hk 421. 4419. 12.0 3 2 vietnam 357. 1128. 3.47 2 3 thailand 1052. 1583. 1.52 2 4 malaysia 4363. 4624. 1.08 1 5 china 4260. 4570. 1.04 1 6 south_korea 1931. 1604. 0.905 2 7 usa 4092. 3318. 0.830 1 8 japan 2524. 1835. 0.740 2 9 china-tw 3131. 1793. 0.685 1 ``` ::: ::: Step 8: Interactive plot ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} country_table <- country_features %>% mutate( avg_input = round(avg_input, 2), avg_output = round(avg_output, 2), avg_balance = round(avg_balance, 2), avg_ratio = round(avg_ratio, 2) ) %>% select(country, avg_input, avg_output, avg_balance, avg_ratio, cluster) datatable(country_table) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
